source.title: The ERP correlates of self-knowledge in ageing.

confidence_rationale: Direct evidence from the Renoult 'personal semantics' programme that self/personal knowledge is neurally dissociable from both general semantic and episodic memory, yet the distinctiveness is GRADED (it dedifferentiates in ageing and scales with episodic memory function). A graded, degree-of-distinctiveness picture supports the ABM-1 'tag not type' decision (autobiographical = self/affect-tagged content on a continuum) over a categorically separate store. Moderate confidence: ERP component dissociations are indirect about storage architecture, and the mapping from human cognitive neuroscience to a memory-type taxonomy claim carries transfer risk.
failure_signatures: In older adults the late-positive-component differentiation between self-knowledge, general semantic, and episodic conditions disappeared, i.e. the 'distinct' personal-semantic signature is not architecturally fixed but depends on episodic memory integrity -- a fully first-class separate type would not be expected to collapse this way.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Self-knowledge (a form of personal semantic knowledge) has neural correlates dissociable from general semantic and episodic memory in young adults, but these correlates lose their distinctiveness ('dedifferentiate') in ageing, with the degree of differentiation tracking individual episodic memory function.
mapping.ree_translation: Maps to Q-060's resolved sub-question: autobiographical content behaves as a self/affect-tagged layer ON the episodic store (ARC-085 over ARC-007), whose distinctiveness is a graded property of tag strength, rather than a categorically distinct first-class memory type with its own store.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Personal semantics (stable trait self-knowledge) is not identical to autobiographical EVENT memory -- it is the semanticised, de-tagged end of the continuum. The paper evidences gradedness of the self/semantic/episodic boundary, not specifically that life-event memory is a tag rather than a type; it constrains the taxonomy without settling the event-memory case.
mapping.source_context: Human ERP study, 28 young + 26 older adults, trait self-relevance vs general-semantic vs episodic recognition conditions.

confidence_components.notes: Solid peer-reviewed ERP study from the group that originated the personal-semantics framework; transfer risk is the dominant discount because Q-060 is an architecture/taxonomy decision, not a neural-correlate question.
